Robert Zammataro, COO of Water Systems for JEA, presented the Water First North Florida project. He said the project began with the enactment of SB 64 in June 2021, which sought to remove all wastewater plant effluent from the state's surface water. He said the initiative was estimated to cost $2 billion and would have had a significant financial impact. He added that there is current legislation governing minimum flow levels (MFLs) for Ichetucknee and Santa Fe. He said both bodies of water are in recovery, which affects groundwater and water wells. 

Mr. Zammataro said that North Florida is at a crossroads where we can no longer continue to pump groundwater indefinitely. He said that no individual community can solve this problem alone, as the impacts are regional. Recognizing these challenges, a partnership was established in April 2023 among regional utility organizations and water management districts, including the St. Johns River Water Management District, the Suwannee River Water Management District, JEA, GRU, the Clay County Utility Authority, and St. Johns County. He said that over the past two years, they have reviewed more than 1,000 projects and solutions to improve MFLs. He then played a video that explained the Water First project.
